formula: sum(x*x/max for E,S,D; x for the other seven criteria) + T
scope: Four nominated main book records; auxiliary search results, other-book widgets, bibliographies and verification reviews do not expand the discovery corpus.

entries.title: Gunpowder and Galleys
entries.subtitle: Changing Technology and Mediterranean Warfare at Sea in the Sixteenth Century
entries.author: John F. Guilmartin Jr.

criteria.name: Evidence and inferential integrity
criteria.assessment: Detailed historical reconstruction and physical constraints; missing powder supply analysis and incomplete access to adverse reviews prevent higher attainment.

criteria.name: Systems integration
criteria.assessment: Geography, ship design, labor, prices, armaments and competing strategic commitments form an integrated explanation.

criteria.name: Transferable strategic utility
criteria.assessment: Exceptional reuse in technology adoption, scarce complements, platform choice and procurement strategy.

criteria.name: Mechanistic and causal depth
criteria.assessment: The central question is answered through explicit physical, logistical and economic constraints, not presumed backwardness.

criteria.name: Information density and length justification
criteria.assessment: Alternating cases and analysis earn most of the length; technical appendices and some dry detail cost one raw point.

criteria.name: Durability and resistance to hype
criteria.assessment: A mature historical explanation with no dependence on a current forecast.

criteria.name: Direct domain fit
criteria.assessment: Direct match to strategic technology, resource allocation, quantification and military power.

criteria.name: Expert authority and intellectual standing
criteria.assessment: Specialist standing is supported by serious assessments across three decades, including Moran and Richon.

criteria.name: Narrative architecture and clarity
criteria.assessment: Analytical organization is effective but technical density and endnotes slow reading.

criteria.name: Authorial precision and finesse
criteria.assessment: Careful distinctions between tactics, operational reach and strategic results.

entries.title: The Invisible Weapon
entries.subtitle: Telecommunications and International Politics, 1851–1945
entries.author: Daniel R. Headrick
entries.sourceLabel: Oxford: main book record and contents

criteria.name: Evidence and inferential integrity
criteria.assessment: Documented historical synthesis; strategic effects are not cleanly isolated and peacetime cases are less developed.

criteria.name: Systems integration
criteria.assessment: Links communications engineering, firms, network ownership, commerce, diplomacy and military intelligence.

criteria.name: Transferable strategic utility
criteria.assessment: Reusable account of infrastructure dependence, control points and technological substitution; modern transfer needs judgment.

criteria.name: Mechanistic and causal depth
criteria.assessment: Shows how network access and interception alter options; not a complete causal explanation of diplomatic outcomes.

criteria.name: Information density and length justification
criteria.assessment: A compact chronological account; familiar late-war material reduces marginal value.

criteria.name: Durability and resistance to hype
criteria.assessment: Historical mechanisms survive changes in communications hardware.

criteria.name: Direct domain fit
criteria.assessment: Communications infrastructure, industrial organization and geostrategy directly fit.

criteria.name: Expert authority and intellectual standing
criteria.assessment: Established technology historian; contemporary specialist assessment recognizes the book's substantive contribution.

criteria.name: Narrative architecture and clarity
criteria.assessment: Accessible cumulative narrative, with technology and political changes in an intelligible sequence.

criteria.name: Authorial precision and finesse
criteria.assessment: Rejects a simple technology-determines-politics account; maintains useful conceptual distinctions.

entries.title: Revolution in Time
entries.subtitle: Clocks and the Making of the Modern World
entries.author: David S. Landes
entries.sourceLabel: Harvard book record on Google Books

criteria.name: Evidence and inferential integrity
criteria.assessment: Substantial scholarship and critical specialist praise; broad cultural explanations do not have experimental identification.

criteria.name: Systems integration
criteria.assessment: Connects precision engineering, navigation, production, trade, work discipline and cultural demand.

criteria.name: Transferable strategic utility
criteria.assessment: Strong lessons on standards, manufacturing advantage and industry migration; one industry cannot prove a universal growth model.

criteria.name: Mechanistic and causal depth
criteria.assessment: Explains feedback between demand, precision and production capability; some cultural causal claims remain provisional.

criteria.name: Information density and length justification
criteria.assessment: Technical development and industrial comparison generally earn their space for this reader; unevenness costs one raw point.

criteria.name: Durability and resistance to hype
criteria.assessment: Long historical scope; the value does not rest on dated predictions about electronic watches.

criteria.name: Direct domain fit
criteria.assessment: Precision, technology, industry and civilization are central subjects.

criteria.name: Expert authority and intellectual standing
criteria.assessment: Expert economic historian; Hobsbawm and Golinski supply substantive assessments, not merely publisher blurbs.

criteria.name: Narrative architecture and clarity
criteria.assessment: Three connected parts and clear prose organize a difficult subject; density alone does not make the architecture poor.

criteria.name: Authorial precision and finesse
criteria.assessment: Specialist reviewers identify precise, controlled and lucid historical explanation.

entries.title: How Economics Shapes Science
entries.author: Paula Stephan
entries.sourceLabel: Harvard/JSTOR: main book record, contents and extracts

criteria.name: Evidence and inferential integrity
criteria.assessment: Explicit treatment of uncertainty and counterfactuals; evidence that cuts against a simple marketization critique is retained.

criteria.name: Systems integration
criteria.assessment: Connects careers, laboratories, funding, institutions and economic growth; corporate science receives less attention.

criteria.name: Transferable strategic utility
criteria.assessment: Useful for evaluating research incentives, grant structures and institutional choices.

criteria.name: Mechanistic and causal depth
criteria.assessment: Strong incentive mechanisms; aggregate causal estimates and optimum funding remain unsettled.

criteria.name: Information density and length justification
criteria.assessment: An unusually dense synthesis; some descriptive material slows reading.

criteria.name: Durability and resistance to hype
criteria.assessment: General mechanisms endure, but funding figures and labor-market conditions are period-specific.

criteria.name: Direct domain fit
criteria.assessment: Scientific organization and research allocation directly fit this reader.

criteria.name: Expert authority and intellectual standing
criteria.assessment: Established economics-of-science scholar; specialist reviews engage closely with the evidence.

criteria.name: Narrative architecture and clarity
criteria.assessment: A clear cumulative analysis, though parts read as a descriptive survey.

criteria.name: Authorial precision and finesse
criteria.assessment: Carefully qualified claims and separation of evidence from prescription.
